I just went through something similar. I was exhausted, and my legs weren't recovering (it took well over 4 days for my legs to feel normal again!). I know at the time I was probably too overwhelmed with work, and they gym, and other sports and that contributed to my feeling drained. But I have an inkling that I may be slightly anaemic. It didn't occur to me that it had been awhile since I had some protein other than eggs, and the spinach I had been having probably wasn't enough iron. So I went out got the biggest, fattest steak, bbq'd it very rare. It did the trick.

If you really are lifting and running as much as you say you are, I'm betting you are not getting enough to eat, and on top of that, aren't allowing your body enough time to absorb the nutrients from the food you are not eating.

Have you ever recorded the calories and macros (protein, carbs, fat) for everything you eat for at least a few days? Go to one of those TDEE (total daily energy expenditure) calculators, see what you should be eating, and then compare that with the nutrient intake you have recorded.

One of bodybuilder Jay Cutler's workout guidelines says to eat at least 4 meals between workouts, and it is a pretty decent guideline.

If you are letting your body rest between workouts your not gonna get the results you want. You will push and push and probably injure something. If you are gonna go consecutive days you need a routine built for that. Even PPL is a 3 day workout one day off with time between rests. If your doing like a 531 or 5x5 routine you need a day of rest for your muscles to repair. I would suggest building up to the routine your doing. Your body is telling you everything you need to know.

Workout day 1. Cardio day 2. Just doing this should help for now.

What routine are you running?
What is your goal?
How much sleep are you getting?
Is there alot of stress in your life?

Sure some athletes train twice a day, but, they also rest there body inbetween. They get acupuncture, messages, sauna and steam baths, etc.....

Training the same muscles group on two days back to back, in general is not a good idea. When you train your muscles under resistance (weights, body weight, running etc.) the muscle fibers get what can be described as micro tears;this is a normal response to training. Your body needs to be put under load for it to be stimulated and learn that it needs to grow stronger in order to cope with the new stresses on it.

For your case in particular it sounds like you are not giving your body enough rest between session. As a rule of thumb, if you trained a group of muscles and they feel stiff, sore or weaker then normal then let them rest for 48 to 72 hours so they can recover. Plan your work outs within a week so that all of your muscles get a chance to rest. E.g you might do a back and chest work out on Monday and Thursday, legs on a Tuesday and Sunday and running on a Friday.

Other advice I can give you is to get an adequate amount of protein in your diet, aim to get at least 8 hours of rest, stretch after a work out (a whole discussion of its own really) and drink plenty of water. If at the very least let your tired muscles rest, Rome wasn't built over night and neither will your body be.

As several people have mentioned, recovery takes time, energy, and rest. Under the assumption that you can do back to back workout days, you need to make sure you're getting enough protein to rebuild the damage to the muscles, and that you're sleeping enough. If you're reading properly and sleeping well, then you might need to include stretching, massage, or something into your routine to increase blood flow and encourage recovery. Otherwise, you might want to do a heavy/light routine. Go heavy and Max out on even days, go light and work on form and motion on odd days. You still exercise, but give your body the break to recover that you need.

But first and foremost, quality macros, and good sleeping habits.
